# Adjudication Task — Chapter 258

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃258화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 눈이 뒤집혔다.
  6|
  7|“어디 가! 이 개새끼야!”
  8|
  9|예전 같았다면 갑자기 왜? 라는 생각이 먼저 들었을 것이다. 어쩌면 위기를 모면했다는 생각에 내심 안도의 한숨을 내쉬었을지도 모르겠다.
 10|
 11|그러나 지금은 아니다.
 12|
 13|‘이 새끼, 실컷 때리고 튀어?’
 14|
 15|아직 절정에 머무르고 있는 나와는 달리 종리추는 명실상부한 초절정 고수. 몇 수 위의 실력이라는 것은 인정한다.
 16|
 17|하지만 승부가 나기도 전에 이렇게 가 버리다니.
 18|
 19|나는 이를 악물었다. 쿡쿡 쑤시는 내상을 무시하며 모든 공력을 하체에 집중했다.
 20|
 21|“거기 딱 서라.”
 22|
 23|우지직. 콰앙!
 24|
 25|굉음과 함께 허공으로 도약했다. 서늘한 바람이 얼굴을 때렸고 종리추의 발이 눈앞에 있었다.
 26|
 27|손만 뻗으면 닿을 수 있는 거리. 머릿속에 한 가지 확신이 스쳤다.
 28|
 29|‘잡았다.’
 30|
 31|쉭!
 32|
 33|하지만 회심의 미소를 지으며 내지른 창날은 허무하게 허공을 갈랐다.
 34|
 35|나는 순간 이해가 되지 않아 눈을 깜빡였다.
 36|
 37|‘어떻게?’
 38|
 39|내신 7등급이어도 만유인력의 법칙은 알고 있다. 종리추의 신형은 이미 최고점을 찍고 낙하하는 중이었고, 나는 힘을 받아 올라가는 중이었다.
 40|
 41|분명 맨손으로도 놈의 발목을 잡을 수 있는 거리였다.
 42|
 43|그러나 바로 그 확신에 사로잡혀 가장 중요한 사실을 놓쳤다.
 44|
 45|무림인은, 초절정 고수는 상식을 깨부수는 존재라는 것을.
 46|
 47|“이런 미친…….”
 48|
 49|저절로 벌어진 입술 사이로 욕이 튀어나왔다. 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경은 그만큼 충격적이었다.
 50|
 51|파파팟!
 52|
 53|밟는다. 벽도, 나뭇가지도 존재하지 않는 텅 빈 허공을.
 54|
 55|마치 보이지 않는 계단이라도 있는 것처럼, 종리추는 허공을 밟으며 높게, 더 높게 솟구치고 있었다.
 56|
 57|‘허공답보(虛空踏步)…….’
 58|
 59|이런 개 같은 경우를 봤나. 저걸 어떻게 잡아.
 60|
 61|내심 욕을 중얼거리며 함께 추락하는 내 시야에 혼란에 빠진 사람들의 모습이 들어왔다.
 62|
 63|그 사이에서 차갑게 눈을 빛내는 자그마한 노인도.
 64|
 65|“놈! 감히 어딜!”
 66|
 67|화왕 적천강.
 68|
 69|하늘을 떨어 울리는 그의 노호성과 함께 주름진 손에서 붉은 빛줄기가 솟구쳤다. 극양(極陽)의 공력이 실린 한 자루의 검이 수십 장의 거리를 지우고 표적에 명중했다.
 70|
 71|구구구궁!
 72|
 73|공기의 떨림, 허공에서 터져 나온 섬광이 망막을 찔렀다. 눈을 감았다 뜬 내게 추락하는 종리추의 모습이 보였다.
 74|
 75|아니, 정정해야겠다.
 76|
 77|‘저건 추락이 아니야.’
 78|
 79|안타깝게도 앞서와 달리 이번 예상은 적중했다.
 80|
 81|적천강의 침음성이 증거이고 화살처럼 쏘아지는 종리추의 신형이 그 결과다.
 82|
 83|‘막았다.’
 84|
 85|종리추는 적천강의 검을 막아 냈을 뿐 아니라, 검에 실린 막대한 공력을 추진력 삼아 원하는 방향으로 가속도를 더했다.
 86|
 87|그 짧은 순간 내린 판단이라고는 믿기지 않을 정도로 영리하고 효율적인 선택이었다.
 88|
 89|쐐애애애액!
 90|
 91|까마득히 높은 상공에서 유성처럼 쏘아지는 종리추를 막을 수 있는 것은 이제 아무도 없었다.
 92|
 93|타닥.
 94|
 95|만유인력을 몸소 체험한 내가 초토화된 비무장에 내려앉음과 동시에 적천강의 격노한 음성이 쩌렁쩌렁 울려 퍼졌다.
 96|
 97|“뭣 하느냐! 당장 놈을 쫓아라!”
 98|
 99|워낙 창졸간에 벌어진 일. 적천강의 일갈에 비로소 현실을 인지한 상석의 수뇌부가 움직였다.
100|
101|“상승검 종리추를 잡아라!”
102|
103|“흉계를 꾸미고 있는 마교의 간세를 포박하라! 생사 여부를 불문하고 놈을 잡는 자에게는 큰 상을 내리겠다!”
104|
105|구파일방과 오대세가. 거기에 더해 각 성에서 큰 영향력을 발휘하는 유력 문파들까지. 이 자리에 모인 이들은 모두 무림을 움직이는 핵심 인물이다.
106|
107|당연히 그들의 수행원도 내로라하는 절정 고수로 이루어져 있을 수밖에 없었다.
108|
109|“존명!”
110|
111|사방으로 흩어지는 수백의 무인들. 그 선두에는 나와 적천강, 그리고 벽력도왕을 비롯한 몇몇 수뇌부가 있었다.
112|
113|쐐애애애액!
114|
115|우리는 그 누구보다 앞서 나갔다. 열화문의 독문 신법인 염화일로(炎火一路)를 9성까지 익힌 적천강과 나란히 설 수는 없었지만, 등을 보며 따라갈 정도는 되었다.
116|
117|‘이가 없으면 잇몸이지.’
118|
119|비록 신법의 경지도 낮고, 무공도 아직 절정 끝자락에 머물러 있지만 이미 한계를 벗어던진 신체 능력은 그것을 가능케 했다.
120|
121|“내상은, 괜찮으냐?”
122|
123|“버틸 만합니다.”
124|
125|세찬 바람 소리 너머로 들려오는 적천강의 말에 고개를 끄덕인 그때였다.
126|
127|띠링.
128|
129|
130|
131|- 규칙에 따라 먼저 비무장을 벗어난 [???]이 장외 패 처리되었습니다!
132|
133|- 퀘스트, [성라대연]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
134|
135|- 위대한 업적, [성라대연 우승]을 달성하셨습니다!
136|
137|- 참가자들의 수준과 대회 난이도에 따라 차등 보상이 지급됩니다!
138|
139|- 막대한 경험치와 명성, 추가 포인트를 획득했습니다!
140|
141|- 레벨 업!
142|
143|- 레벨 업!
144|
145|- 레벨 업!
146|
147|.
148|
149|.
150|
151|.
152|
153|
154|
155|띠링. 띠링. 띠링.
156|
157|쉴 새 없이 귓가를 파고드는 시스템 알림과 함께 변화가 시작되었다.
158|
159|지쳐 있던 육신에 활력이 깃들었고, 폐부를 쿡쿡 찌르던 내상은 말끔하게 치유되었다. 전력을 다한 공방으로 힘을 잃었던 단전의 화룡이 용틀임하며 사지 백해로 뻗어 나갔다.
160|
161|‘이런 식으로 성라대연에서 우승하게 될 줄이야.’
162|
163|그러나 내게는 시스템 메시지를 확인할 여유 따위는 주어지지 않았다.
164|
165|앞서 사라진 종리추를 찾는 것이 급선무였기 때문이다.
166|
167|“빌어먹을, 어떤 놈인지 몰라도 발 한번 더럽게 빠르군.”
168|
169|개방 방주이자 경공술의 대가인 만리추행(萬里追行)의 말처럼 종리추는 상상을 초월할 정도로 빨랐다.
170|
171|이미 놈의 모습은 모두의 시야에서 벗어난 지 오래. 적천강이 빠르게 지시를 내렸다.
172|
173|“이대로는 놈을 놓친다. 개방이 서쪽을 맡고 곤륜파와 나머지는 그 사이사이를 채워.”
174|
175|“예, 적 대협.”
176|
177|“알겠습니다.”
178|
179|파팟!
180|
181|개방과 곤륜파. 신법으로 이름 높은 두 문파의 장문인이 휘하 제자를 이끌고 사라지자 적천강이 벽력도왕을 응시했다.
182|
183|“자네는 동쪽일세.”
184|
185|“그럼 이곳은?”
186|
187|“노부가 맡아야지.”
188|
189|벽력도왕이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
190|
191|“조심하게. 상승검인지 뭔지 하는 그놈…… 혼자서는 감당하기 버거울 거야.”
192|
193|감당하기 버겁다?
194|
195|자존심 세기로는 둘째가면 서럽다는 벽력도왕의 입에서 나온 말이다.
196|
197|해석하자면 종리추가 십왕에 견줄 만한, 혹은 그 이상의 고수라는 뜻이기도 했다.
198|
199|‘종리추가 그 정도였다니.’
200|
201|어떻게 그 나이에 저만한 경지를 이룬 걸까.
202|
203|괴물도 이런 괴물이 따로 없다. 내가 놀라움을 삼키고 있을 때 적천강이 코웃음 치며 말했다.
204|
205|“그거야 자네 같은 하수들한테나 해당하는 말이고. 노부를 같은 급으로 치면 안 되지.”
206|
207|농담처럼 말했지만, 그 역시 벽력도왕의 말을 허투루 넘겨 듣지 않았음이 분명하다.
208|
209|올라간 입꼬리와는 달리 적천강의 눈은 차갑게 가라앉아 있었으니까.
210|
211|“군소리는 그만하면 됐으니 이제 가 봐.”
212|
213|“제기랄. 하늘도 무심하시지. 하필 이럴 때 굉도, 이 땡중은 도대체 어딜 간 거야?”
214|
215|외마디 한탄을 남긴 벽력도왕이 발걸음을 틀어 시야에서 사라졌다.
216|
217|이제 남은 사람은 적천강과 나, 둘 뿐이었다.
218|
219|우리는 빠른 속도로 끊임없이 늘어선 수백여 채의 건물을 넘고 지나치며 말을 주고받았다.
220|
221|“놈을 발견하거든 경거망동하지 말거라. 알겠느냐?”
222|
223|“장담은 못 하겠네요. 갚아 줄 게 있어서.”
224|
225|“종리추는 네가 상대할 수 없는 고수다. 노부의 명이 있기 전까지는 절대 나서지 마라.”
226|
227|“도대체 얼마나 강한 겁니까?”
228|
229|잠깐의 침묵 끝에 적천강의 입술이 열렸다.
230|
231|“모른다.”
232|
233|“그 말씀은…….”
234|
235|“놈이 어떤 무공을 익혔는지, 어느 정도의 경지에 다다랐는지 노부의 눈으로도 파악할 수 없었다.”
236|
237|“……!”
238|
239|자존심 강한 벽력도왕에 이어, 무력으로는 십왕 중에서도 첫손에 꼽는 적천강마저 이런 대답을 내놓다니.
240|
241|바짝 마른 입술을 핥은 그 순간이었다.
242|
243|콰과과광!
244|
245|저 멀리, 굉음과 함께 먼지 구름이 솟아올랐다. 사람들의 비명과 호각 소리가 사방에서 울리며 적의 출현을 알렸다.
246|
247|나는 활짝 열린 감각으로 정보를 받아들였다.
248|
249|‘서쪽, 오백여 장 밖.’
250|
251|개방이 있는 방향이다.
252|
253|전력을 기울여 신법을 발휘한다면 촌각 만에 도달할 수 있는 거리이기도 했다.
254|
255|“노야!”
256|
257|“알고 있다.”
258|
259|콰아앙!
260|
261|적천강과 나는 포탄처럼 쏘아졌다.
262|
263|걸음을 내디딜 때마다 휙휙 스쳐 가던 주위 풍경이 바뀌기 시작했다. 끝없이 늘어서 있던 전각이 하나둘씩 줄어들었고 높게 솟은 성벽이 모습을 드러냈다.
264|
265|거센 풍압을 거스르며 달릴수록 가슴이 한구석이 묵직해져 왔다.
266|
267|‘뭐지, 이 느낌은?’
268|
269|설마 종리추와 다시 대면한다는 중압감 때문일까?
270|
271|힐끗 옆을 곁눈질하자 딱딱하게 굳은 적천강의 표정이 보였다. 그의 얼굴에 서린 것은 명백한 불길함이었다.
272|
273|그리고 잠시 후, 우리는 그 설명할 수 없는 감정의 실체를 확인할 수 있었다.
274|
275|“놈을 쫓아라!”
276|
277|“대사(大師)! 정신 차리십시오, 대사!”
278|
279|폭만 삼십여 장에 달하는 거대한 구덩이. 모여 있는 개방의 제자들 사이로 피에 젖은 가사(袈裟)가 드러났다.
280|
281|간헐적으로 떨리는 주름진 손. 잘려 나간 두 다리 밑에는 피 웅덩이가 고여 있었고, 주인의 피로 붉게 물든 염주 알이 그 위를 둥둥 떠다녔다.
282|
283|“……땡중?”
284|
285|친우를 발견한 적천강의 발걸음이 우뚝 멎었다.
286|
287|
288|
289|* * *
290|
291|
292|
293|적천강은 눈앞이 아득해졌다.
294|
295|귓가에 마지막으로 나눴던 대화가 끊임없이 맴돌았다.
296|
297|
298|
299|‘일이 생겼네. 잠시 자리를 비워야겠어.’
300|
301|‘지금?’
302|
303|‘금방 처리하고 옴세.’
304|
305|‘작은 거야, 큰 거야?’
306|
307|‘아미타불. 석가께서 이르시길 큰일을 먼저 해결하면 작은 일도 해결된다 하셨지.’
308|
309|‘그놈의 아미타불은. 그러니까 자네가 땡중 소리 듣는 걸세.’
310|
311|‘부처면 어떻고, 땡중이면 어떤가? 허허허.’
312|
313|
314|
315|반 시진 전, 웃음과 함께 자리를 떴던 그의 모습을 똑똑히 기억한다. 그런데 왜…….
316|
317|‘왜 여기서 이러고 있나.’
318|
319|철벅.
320|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 258

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃258화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 눈이 뒤집혔다.
  6|
  7|“어디 가! 이 개새끼야!”
  8|
  9|예전 같았다면 갑자기 왜? 라는 생각이 먼저 들었을 것이다. 어쩌면 위기를 모면했다는 생각에 내심 안도의 한숨을 내쉬었을지도 모르겠다.
 10|
 11|그러나 지금은 아니다.
 12|
 13|‘이 새끼, 실컷 때리고 튀어?’
 14|
 15|아직 절정에 머무르고 있는 나와는 달리 종리추는 명실상부한 초절정 고수. 몇 수 위의 실력이라는 것은 인정한다.
 16|
 17|하지만 승부가 나기도 전에 이렇게 가 버리다니.
 18|
 19|나는 이를 악물었다. 쿡쿡 쑤시는 내상을 무시하며 모든 공력을 하체에 집중했다.
 20|
 21|“거기 딱 서라.”
 22|
 23|우지직. 콰앙!
 24|
 25|굉음과 함께 허공으로 도약했다. 서늘한 바람이 얼굴을 때렸고 종리추의 발이 눈앞에 있었다.
 26|
 27|손만 뻗으면 닿을 수 있는 거리. 머릿속에 한 가지 확신이 스쳤다.
 28|
 29|‘잡았다.’
 30|
 31|쉭!
 32|
 33|하지만 회심의 미소를 지으며 내지른 창날은 허무하게 허공을 갈랐다.
 34|
 35|나는 순간 이해가 되지 않아 눈을 깜빡였다.
 36|
 37|‘어떻게?’
 38|
 39|내신 7등급이어도 만유인력의 법칙은 알고 있다. 종리추의 신형은 이미 최고점을 찍고 낙하하는 중이었고, 나는 힘을 받아 올라가는 중이었다.
 40|
 41|분명 맨손으로도 놈의 발목을 잡을 수 있는 거리였다.
 42|
 43|그러나 바로 그 확신에 사로잡혀 가장 중요한 사실을 놓쳤다.
 44|
 45|무림인은, 초절정 고수는 상식을 깨부수는 존재라는 것을.
 46|
 47|“이런 미친…….”
 48|
 49|저절로 벌어진 입술 사이로 욕이 튀어나왔다. 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경은 그만큼 충격적이었다.
 50|
 51|파파팟!
 52|
 53|밟는다. 벽도, 나뭇가지도 존재하지 않는 텅 빈 허공을.
 54|
 55|마치 보이지 않는 계단이라도 있는 것처럼, 종리추는 허공을 밟으며 높게, 더 높게 솟구치고 있었다.
 56|
 57|‘허공답보(虛空踏步)…….’
 58|
 59|이런 개 같은 경우를 봤나. 저걸 어떻게 잡아.
 60|
 61|내심 욕을 중얼거리며 함께 추락하는 내 시야에 혼란에 빠진 사람들의 모습이 들어왔다.
 62|
 63|그 사이에서 차갑게 눈을 빛내는 자그마한 노인도.
 64|
 65|“놈! 감히 어딜!”
 66|
 67|화왕 적천강.
 68|
 69|하늘을 떨어 울리는 그의 노호성과 함께 주름진 손에서 붉은 빛줄기가 솟구쳤다. 극양(極陽)의 공력이 실린 한 자루의 검이 수십 장의 거리를 지우고 표적에 명중했다.
 70|
 71|구구구궁!
 72|
 73|공기의 떨림, 허공에서 터져 나온 섬광이 망막을 찔렀다. 눈을 감았다 뜬 내게 추락하는 종리추의 모습이 보였다.
 74|
 75|아니, 정정해야겠다.
 76|
 77|‘저건 추락이 아니야.’
 78|
 79|안타깝게도 앞서와 달리 이번 예상은 적중했다.
 80|
 81|적천강의 침음성이 증거이고 화살처럼 쏘아지는 종리추의 신형이 그 결과다.
 82|
 83|‘막았다.’
 84|
 85|종리추는 적천강의 검을 막아 냈을 뿐 아니라, 검에 실린 막대한 공력을 추진력 삼아 원하는 방향으로 가속도를 더했다.
 86|
 87|그 짧은 순간 내린 판단이라고는 믿기지 않을 정도로 영리하고 효율적인 선택이었다.
 88|
 89|쐐애애애액!
 90|
 91|까마득히 높은 상공에서 유성처럼 쏘아지는 종리추를 막을 수 있는 것은 이제 아무도 없었다.
 92|
 93|타닥.
 94|

[P137]
Their last conversation echoed endlessly in his ears.

[P138]
*“Something came up. I need to step away for a while.”*

[P139]
*“Now?”*

[P140]
*“I’ll take care of it and be right back.”*

[P141]
*“Is it something small or something serious?”*

[P142]
*“Amitabha. As Shakyamuni said, if you resolve the greater matter first, the smaller matter will resolve itself.”*

[P143]
*“That damn Amitabha. This is why people call you a damn monk.”*

[P144]
*“What does it matter whether I’m a Buddha or a damn monk? Ha-ha-ha.”*

[P145]
He remembered clearly how Hong Dao had left with a laugh half a shichen ago.

[P146]
But why…?

[P147]
*Why are you lying here like this?*

[P148]
Splash.

[P149]
Mud and bloody water splattered. The Beggars’ Sect disciples surrounding the fallen old monk hurriedly stepped aside and bowed their heads.

[P150]
“G-Great Hero Jeok!”

[P151]
“Our Sect Leader is pursuing Jongni Chu. B-but by the time we arrived, it was already too late…”

[P152]
“Move.”

[P153]
The voice that slipped from Jeok Cheongang’s lips was as dry as spent ash.

[P154]
Every sound stopped. It was as though the world itself had frozen.

[P155]
His senses were already focused on one person alone.

[P156]
“I’m here.”

[P157]
It was the same greeting as always. But instead of Hong Dao’s sly voice, a labored cough answered him.

[P158]
Cough. Cough.

[P159]
The Dharma King Hong Dao’s chest heaved, and black blood spilled from the corner of his mouth.

[P160]
A grave Internal Injury. Fragments of his organs were mixed into the blood. There was no need to examine him to know what had happened inside his body.

[P161]
“Well, now. Your friend is here, and you couldn’t even wait for me before lying down again?”

[P162]
Jeok Cheongang spoke calmly as he dropped down beside Hong Dao.

[P163]
He grasped the blood-soaked old monk’s wrist and sent internal energy into him. What he had suspected became reality.

[P164]
*Beyond saving.*

[P165]
The painful, crushing verdict filled Jeok Cheongang’s mind.

[P166]
“Do you remember when we first met? Back when we fought those Demonic Cult bastards in Gansu almost every day?”

[P167]
Was Hong Dao listening? Could he even hear him?

[P168]
Everyone wondered the same thing, but Jeok Cheongang paid them no mind and continued.

[P169]
“At first, I wondered what kind of damn monk you were. But even bad blood can become a bond. When the time came for us to part, I found myself reluctant to see you go.”

[P170]
Although he had never once said it aloud, Hong Dao was the only friend Jeok Cheongang had ever opened his heart to.

[P171]
To his Master, he had needed to be a reliable Disciple. To the first Disciple he later accepted, he had needed to be a dependable Master.

[P172]
But Hong Dao was different.

[P173]
When he was with Hong Dao, he did not have to be anyone’s anything. He could simply be Jeok Cheongang, an ordinary human being.

[P174]
“Did you know?”

[P175]
Jeok Cheongang sent internal energy into Hong Dao’s Mingmen acupoint and spoke in a low voice.

[P176]
“You are my dearest friend.”

[P177]
The breath that had seemed ready to fail at any moment eased. Eyelids that looked as though they would remain closed forever slowly opened.

[P178]
A final rally.

[P179]
Jeok Cheongang gazed into Hong Dao’s gray eyes as the final flame of life flickered within them.

[P180]
“Speak. Anything at all.”

[P181]
Hong Dao’s blood-soaked lips moved faintly. Jeok Cheongang put his ear to Hong Dao’s mouth and listened to his final words, his expression changing by the moment.

[P182]
Anger. Shock. A sudden realization.

[P183]
And the final emotion to appear was sorrow.

[P184]
Rustle. Thud.

[P185]
The coughing voice fell silent. The heaving chest and trembling eyelids settled peacefully.

[P186]
Hong Dao closed his eyes as though drifting off to sleep, a satisfied smile resting on his lips.

[P187]
Jeok Cheongang stared at him for a long moment, then spoke.

[P188]
“We’re going to Shaolin.”

[P189]
His voice boiled like molten lava.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
